=== FINDING 1 (CONFIRMED, reproduced at BOTH heads, blocking) -- the workflow safety test is vacuous ===
tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py::test_the_workflow_never_checks_out_pull_request_code_under_a_write_token claims: 'This test fails the moment those two facts coexist.' It does not. It cannot.
  pins_default_branch = 'default_branch' in workflow
is a substring search over the ENTIRE file text, and the literal string 'default_branch' already appears in the file -- in the explanatory COMMENT at .github/workflows/lwb-auto-queue.yml line 63 ('ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}'). pins_default_branch is therefore True today and stays True while that comment exists, whatever the checkout step actually does, so the assertion 'not triggers_on_pr or pins_default_branch' short-circuits to pass unconditionally. The guard is satisfied by its own warning comment.
REPRODUCTION (run by me at 8d75890b and again at dd9e1ad; file restored both times, tree left clean):
  1. Added to .github/workflows/lwb-auto-queue.yml, verbatim, after the existing push trigger:
       pull_request:
         branches:
           - main
     leaving 'uses: actions/checkout@v7' UNPINNED and 'permissions: pull-requests: write' untouched -- exactly the state the comment above the checkout step calls dangerous.
  2. python -m pytest tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py::test_the_workflow_never_checks_out_pull_request_code_under_a_write_token -q
     -> '1 passed in 0.01s', at both heads.
A PR-controlled checkout under a pull-requests:write token would ship with a green suite.
SUGGESTED FIX (behavioural, not cosmetic): assert on the checkout step's real 'with.ref' value, or at minimum strip comment lines before the substring test. Then re-run the mutation above and show the test FAIL. A guard never seen to fail on the thing it guards is not evidence.

=== FINDING 6 (CONFIRMED, new at this head) -- both gates accept a proof record that says in its own value that nobody checked it ===
proof/29.json, added by dd9e1ad, carries:
  author     = 'lw-architect-opus5-af50c414-2026-09-19'
  checked_by = 'UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review'
scripts/lwb_check_proof.py validates checked_by only as (a) a non-empty string and (b) != author (lines 147-150). The literal string 'UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review' satisfies both. Measured: `python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 29` exits 0, 'lwb-proof check passed (19 record(s))'. scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py::readiness applies the SAME two tests and nothing more, so it too would count this as a satisfied proof record and raise no objection -- I verified the predicate directly against the real file.
This is the 'cannot distinguish I-checked-and-found-nothing from I-could-not-check' shape, at the data layer rather than the control-flow layer: the one record whose entire job is to attest that a human or peer checked the work is satisfied by a value that declares the opposite.
TO BE FAIR TO THE AUTHOR: writing a visible placeholder instead of inventing a checker name is the honest choice, and I am not calling it deceptive. The defect is that the GATES accept it. Fix: reject a checked_by matching a placeholder/unchecked sentinel, or require it to parse as an identity the way reviews records' ids must.
RELATED, and worth correcting on the PR: the PR body still states 'There is no proof/<pr>.json either, because checked_by must differ from author and no one has checked it yet.' That is no longer true of the tree -- the record exists and passes the gate.

=== FINDING 2 (CONFIRMED, non-blocking today, but the script overclaims) -- review_records() accepts records lwb_lanes.py rejects ===
scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py's docstring says it 'can tell that a review record exists, is AGREE, names a different identity and points at this exact head.' The staleness test is:
    if not head.startswith(reviewed):
with reviewed = str(record.get('reviewed_commit', '')). head.startswith('') is True in Python, and there is no length floor -- unlike scripts/lwb_lanes.py::_review_ok, which requires isinstance str and len(reviewed_commit) >= 7.
REPRODUCTION (my probe, driving aq.review_records(7, 'a'*40) with _list_dir/_contents_json stubbed). Every one of these was ACCEPTED, good=1, problems=[]:
  - reviewed_commit MISSING entirely
  - reviewed_commit = ''
  - reviewed_commit = 'a' (one character)
  - commit_author_id MISSING (author becomes '', so 'reviewer == author' is never true and the independence test is vacuous for that record)
  - reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author = true (an ADMITTED self-review; auto_queue never reads the field and does not even print the NOTICE lwb_lanes.py prints -- the 'reads one field, ignores the sibling field that changes the meaning' shape)
  - reviewer_id / commit_author_id sharing an 8-character token (lwb_lanes.py rejects this via MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH)
  - ids in a format lwb_lanes.py rejects for pr >= REVIEWER_ID_FORMAT_CUTOFF_PR
  - a record whose own 'pr' field says 999 while sitting in reviews/7/ (lwb_lanes.py reconciles this; auto_queue does not)
WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKING, stated so the finding is not overstated: I checked whether auto_queue is the only defence and it is NOT. 'lwb-lanes' is a STEP inside ci.yml's 'test' job (ci.yml line 198), not a standalone check, and the six 'test (<os>, <python>)' contexts ARE required by the live ruleset. readiness() requires every required context to be 'success', so a record only auto_queue accepts still fails lwb-lanes, reddens the test job, and blocks the enqueue. The defect is a second, weaker copy of a gate -- defence-in-depth that is not -- plus a docstring claiming a head-pinning property the code lacks. Fix: reuse the >= 7 floor and the isinstance check, or import from lwb_lanes instead of restating.

=== FINDING 3 (CONFIRMED, latent, fails in the SAFE direction) -- required_contexts() ignores a ruleset's enforcement mode and its branch matcher ===
required_contexts() walks repos/{REPO}/rulesets and collects every required_status_checks context from every ruleset, reading neither 'enforcement' (active|evaluate|disabled) nor 'conditions.ref_name.include'.
REPRODUCTION: I stubbed _gh_json with two rulesets -- one active on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH requiring 'test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)', one with enforcement 'disabled' targeting refs/heads/experiment/* requiring 'never-runs-on-main'. required_contexts() returned ['never-runs-on-main', 'test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)'] -- it inherited a check from a DISABLED ruleset for a DIFFERENT branch.
NO LIVE IMPACT TODAY: I read the real rulesets. There is exactly one (id 23627212, name 'main', enforcement 'active', conditions ref_name include ['~DEFAULT_BRANCH']). The error direction is over-strict: an inherited context never reports, readiness says 'has not reported', the queue stalls. It cannot make auto_queue enqueue something it should not. Recorded because the PR's stated design property is 'read live from the ruleset, so this script cannot drift away from what actually gates main', and a disabled ruleset for another branch is precisely a thing that does not gate main.

=== FINDING 4 (CONFIRMED, low severity) -- dispatch input interpolated into a run: line under a write token ===
.github/workflows/lwb-auto-queue.yml line 84 interpolates ${{ github.event.inputs.pr }} directly into the shell text of a run: step, in a job holding pull-requests: write. GitHub substitutes the value into the script before bash parses it, so an input containing a quote and a semicolon executes as shell. LOW severity because workflow_dispatch requires write access, so the actor is already privileged -- not an escalation, just a bad pattern beside a write token. Fix: pass via env: and use "$PR".

=== OBSERVED, PRE-EXISTING, EXPLICITLY NOT THIS PR'S DEFECT ===
The lwb-lanes step in ci.yml carries "if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'", and ci.yml has an 'on: merge_group:' trigger. In a merge-queue run github.event_name is 'merge_group', so the lane and review gate is SKIPPED while the required 'test (...)' contexts still report success. The gate binds at the PR head, not in the queue. This predates this PR; recorded, not charged to it.
